content:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: 5xx spike for tenant=acme on eu-west dedicated pool. Error rate 18% over 2m.

Sasha (oncall): on it. acked the page. pulling metrics and recent deploys.

Sasha (oncall): @Mira can you ping ACME oncall to warn we might shift traffic?

Mira (acct-mgr): pinged ACME-SRE on phone + slack. they said they can be available for cutover.

Sasha (oncall): grabbing logs — eu-west nodes showing OOM-ish GC stalls and elevated latency. Not an application deploy.

Alberto (sre-lead): if it's dedicated pool resource saturation we should do regional failover to us-east-warm we already keep for ACME. Runbook: reduce DNS TTL, activate warm pool, shift weights, then verify.

Kai (infra): warm capacity currently at 60% pre-warmed. can spin to 100% in ~3m.

Sasha (oncall): executing warm activation via admin API now:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/admin/pools/activate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
  -d 'tenant=acme' -d 'pool=us-east-warm'
```

OpsBot: Task started: activate_pool acme us-east-warm (task_id=AK_4421).

PagerDuty: Sasha acknowledged the incident (P1) — escalation path intact.

ACME-SRE: thanks. we're standing by. please confirm expected downtime or degraded behavior.

Sasha (oncall): aim is no app-level downtime — we'll shift traffic gradually. might see tail latency increase during cutover for some sessions.

Sasha (oncall): next step lowering DNS TTL (Route53) to 60s to speed cutover. Alberto, want me to do UI or you prefer API?

Alberto (sre-lead): I'll do API. Use change-batch with weighted policy. Also create a health-check failover so we can flip if health ok.

Alberto (sre-lead): running TTL update:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.acme.prod.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west","Weight":70,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"35.206.12.4"}]}}]}'
```

Kai (infra): us-east warm pool is at 100% now. verified all healthy and KV cache primed for ACME prefix.

Sasha (oncall): switching weights to 30 eu-west / 70 us-east to start draining eu-west.

Alberto (sre-lead): nice. watch 5xx, p50/p95 latency and tail. If 5xx drops then continue to 0/100 over 10 minutes.

Sasha (oncall): performed weight update via DNS provider UI. monitoring.

OpsBot: Metric update: acme 5xx -> 10% (1m), p95 latency eu-west 1.2s -> overall p95 820ms.

ACME-SRE: seeing improvement on our end for most requests. we still get occasional 502 on long streaming sessions.

Sasha (oncall): streaming sessions rely on sticky KV cache in eu-west. we'll gracefully drain long lived sessions: new sessions go to us-east, existing to finish.

Mira (acct-mgr): ACME wants a timeline and confirmation that their VPC peering won't be impacted.

Kai (infra): VPC peering remains intact — regional routing is via our outbound NATs; no changes to peering. Confirmed private link endpoints available in us-east for ACME.

Alberto (sre-lead): plan for full cutover if 5xx <2% and p95 stable for 5m: move to 0/100 eu-west/us-east and mark eu-west nodes for investigation.

Sasha (oncall): agreed. continuing to monitor. documenting steps in incident doc.

(7m later)

OpsBot: Metric update: acme 5xx -> 2.1% (5m). p95 overall 420ms.

Sasha (oncall): pushing final 0/100 change now.

Alberto (sre-lead): make sure we update customer-facing status page and note planned maintenance window while we root cause the eu-west pool.

Mira (acct-mgr): updated ACME and posted message on status.acme.redwood.com with timeline + contact.

ACME-SRE: all good, traffic fully on us-east for us. thanks for the quick response. can you share postmortem when stable?

Sasha (oncall): yes. I'll capture timeline, metrics, and bespoke mitigation steps (warm pool activation, dns-weight shift, sticky session drain).

Alberto (sre-lead): taking over investigation into eu-west dedicated nodes (heap tuning + kernel logs). Sasha, handoff to me in 20m?

Sasha (oncall): handing off. I'll add handoff summary to thread: actions taken, timestamps, runbook refs, contact list.

Sasha (oncall): HANDOFF -> Alberto at 1750002454 UTC. On-call notes: active mitigations = us-east-warm, DNS TTL=60, weighted DNS failover in place, ACME notified.

Alberto (sre-lead): ack. I'll continue RCF and book a follow-up with ACME's infra team.

OpsBot: Incident state updated: mitigation=regional-failover (acme), severity=P1 -> monitoring.

(end thread)
